2P-proc · benchmark branch · validation report

Tracking cells across sessions

Which method should the pipeline use to match the same neurons across separately processed sessions, and how reliable is it? Five methods were compared on one set of Suite2p footprints with three kinds of evidence: known deformations, a same-day reference and real cross-day data with controls.

Written for the Wang lab 2P group (Vincent, Manuel). Data: Scnn1aAi14_D1M2, 08/24, 08/28, 08/29 (run1, run2) and 08/31 2026; 16×, 765 × 765 px, 1.45 µm/px. Tools: CaImAn 1.12.2, Track2p 0.6.2, ROICaT 1.7.12, CellReg 1.6.0 (MATLAB 2024a on Engaging).

Summary

ROICaT is the pipeline defaultPerfect recovery under known deformations up to 10 µm, the most cross-day matches with the best cycle consistency (0.96), matched cells respond alike, and it refuses to match a different imaging plane.
CellReg is good only while rigid alignment holdsIts rigid mode matches ROICaT on the same day, over 2 days and up to 3 µm of deformation, then rejects the alignment (6 µm, 5-day pairs). Its non-rigid mode misses most pairs (recall 0.25–0.64 under rotation and shift).
The current CaImAn path is weakerIt misses matches as deformation grows (F1 0.83 at 10 µm), finds 11–22% fewer cross-day matches and has cycle consistency 0.81.
Real deformation is small hereAcross 2–5 days, matched cells sit within 0.9–1.9 µm of an affine fit. Non-rigid B-spline alignment (Track2p non-rigid) overfits on real cross-day images and fails.
Segmentation limits trackingEven within one recording, only 57–65% of iscell ROIs have a clear partner when the halves are segmented separately. Same-day runs should be processed jointly.

1 · What existed

Two registration paths existed and neither was used downstream. Caiman/multisession_registration.py runs CaImAn register_multisession on CNMF outputs only; its --json mode cannot read current configs and no parameter is exposed. The MATLAB CellReg wrapper cannot run (undefined variables, returns the initial rather than the final map, relies on a fork-only API, nothing writes its inputs, CellReg is not installed). In practice same-day runs are matched by concatenating them before processing.

2 · Known deformations (split-half)

Suite2p was run separately on the two halves (4000 frames each) of D1M2 run1, which share one motion-corrected frame. Mutual best IoU ≥ 0.5 between the halves defines 370 reference pairs (ROIs with best IoU 0.2–0.5 are not scored). The second half was then deformed with known smooth random fields (150 µm scale), a 1.5° rotation and a 13 µm shift, and every method had to recover the reference pairs.

ROICaT misses 9% of pairs when the two frames are identical (no deformation at all), which does not occur with real data.

3 · Same day, against a joint reference

Runs 1 and 2 of 08/29 were processed separately and jointly (concatenated). Each run's ROIs were mapped onto the joint ROIs after a rigid shift (mutual best IoU ≥ 0.5); two ROIs that map to the same joint ROI form one of 309 reference pairs.

4 · Across days

There is no ground truth across days, so each method is scored by self-consistency and controls: cycle consistency over 08/24 → 08/29 → 08/31 against 08/24 → 08/31; centroid residual after an affine fit; false matches when session-2 footprints are shifted by 60 µm while its image is kept (no true partner exists); matches to 08/28, recorded at a different depth (stage Z 170.7 vs 160 µm, image correlation 0.20 after alignment); and response similarity of matched cells (laser responses) against their nearest non-matched neighbour.

A left-right flipped session was also tried as a control and discarded: ROICaT's image aligner can undo a mirror image and then matches correctly (307 matches), so a flip is not a valid negative for it. The false matches in the shifted-footprint control are a floor for dense fields when no true partner exists; with true partners present (sections 2 and 3) precision stays above 0.92.

5 · CellReg

Upstream CellReg 1.6.0 (zivlab) was run headless on Engaging compute nodes (validation/registration/cellreg), in both its rigid ("Translations and Rotations", as in the lab's wrapper) and non-rigid modes, on the same footprints. CellReg aligns sessions from the footprint projections only, never from the FOV image. Two consequences:

  • When the rigid alignment is poor (6 and 10 µm deformations, the 5-day pairs, the other plane) CellReg warns that a session "does not resemble the reference session" and cannot continue; these are reported as fails. Refusing the other plane is the correct outcome.
  • Shifting all footprints by 60 µm is a plain translation for CellReg, which it undoes, so its 302 matches in that control are true matches (≈ its 306 matches on the unshifted pair), not false ones.

Its self-assessment is informative. CellReg's expected false-positive fraction, the mean of 1 − P_same over its accepted pairs, is close to the measured error where it works, and it flags its own failures: on the cross-day pairs where non-rigid mode breaks down it expects 33–43% false positives.

The three-session CellReg run needs more memory than the 64 GB requested (dense footprints of 1200 + 860 + 510 ROIs); it will be added when resubmitted.

6 · In the pipeline

python -m pipeline.register_sessions --exports <day1> <day2> ... --out <dir> --method roicat (module modules/cell_registration.py). Inputs are Suite2p iscell ROIs or CNMF components and the mean images. Outputs: cell_registration.npz/.mat with the cells × sessions ROI indices in extraction order (1-based in the .mat, 0 = absent), cell_registration_qc.json (matches and affine residual per session pair, FOV similarity with a warning below 0.5) and a QC figure. ROICaT needs Python ≥ 3.11, so it runs in its own environment (--python or $ROICAT_PYTHON), like Suite2p in production.

7 · Recommendations

  1. Use ROICaT for cross-day registration; keep Track2p affine as a lighter alternative and CaImAn for compatibility. Do not use non-rigid B-spline alignment across days, nor CellReg's non-rigid mode. CellReg's rigid mode is a valid cross-check for sessions a few days apart, and its P_same scores are a useful second opinion.
  2. Process runs from the same day and field jointly (concatenated). Separately processed short runs segment inconsistently (on B2M0 04/22, 262 to 4745 Suite2p ROIs per 1600-frame run).
  3. Check the QC: FOV similarity below 0.5 means a different field or plane; affine residuals above ~3 µm or a low tracked fraction call for a look at the images.
  4. Retire Caiman/multisession_registration.py and the MATLAB CellReg wrapper (upstream CellReg runs as shown in validation/registration/cellreg).

Limits and open items

  • One mouse with a same-FOV series; the cross-day evidence is indirect. Blinded manual annotation of a sample of ROIs (with the mean images and z-stacks) would give a direct cross-day error rate.
  • The tdTomato channel at this depth is diffuse (no labelled somata), so it could not anchor true pairs.
  • Pipeline movies are vertically flipped relative to the raw Bruker frames; overlays of raw data (red channel, z-stacks) must account for it.
  • ROICaT's degenerate-case error (different plane) should be caught and reported as "not the same field".

Reproduce

cd validation; pixi run python registration/bench_splithalf.py <half1> <half2> --out ...
pixi run python registration/bench_sameday.py --runs <run1> <run2> --joint <run1run2> --out ...
pixi run python registration/bench_crossday.py --sessions ... --pairs ... --triplets ... --out ...
pixi run python registration/negative_control.py <plane1> <plane2> --out ...
python3 registration/make_registration_figures.py; python3 registration/build_registration_report.py
